observations.body: Manasseh rebuilds high places, erects Baal and Asherah worship, builds heavenly-host altars in the temple courts, and makes his son pass through fire.
observations.label: Manasseh brings rival altars and a son into Jerusalem

observations.body: The passage presents royal reversal, rival altars, heavenly host, child in fire, divination, temple placement, and bloodshed as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: royal reversal, rival altars, heavenly host, child in fire, divination, temple placement, and bloodshed

observations.body: The passage places temple profanation beside royal reversal, rival altars, heavenly host, child in fire, divination, temple placement, and bloodshed.

payload.posture: Read 2 Kings 21:1–16 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the passage shows these acts as provocation rather than alternative faithful sacrifice
